subject: Request: SDK connection-affinity option + field repro for intermittent streaming disconnects
messages:
From: Sara Ahmed <sara@obsidianhealth.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Cc: obsidian_api@obsidianhealth.com
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Intermittent streaming disconnects during live notes ingestion

Hi Ava / Logan,

We're seeing intermittent disconnects (502 / ECONNRESET) from the SDK when our inference stream runs longer than ~70s. The error pattern shows the client reconnecting, but the server sometimes rejects the resumed session and the client has to start a new session which loses partial context. This is causing dropped audio segments in the live notes flow and customers notice stutters.

Attached: obsidian_streaming_repro.log (sanitized) and a small repro zip with a script that hits your streaming endpoint repeatedly. Repro is easiest when we pin requests to a particular region and hold the connection open with constant token throughput.

Can someone from platform/runtime advise if this sounds like a routing/connection-pool issue vs an SDK reconnection behavior? If the SDK could optionally advertise a persistent connection affinity token (or resume token) that the runtime honors, we could avoid expensive warm starts when the reconnect happens.

Thanks,
Sara Ahmed
Integration Lead — Obsidian Health

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: Sara Ahmed <sara@obsidianhealth.com>, Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intermittent streaming disconnects during live notes ingestion

Sara — thanks for the detailed repro and logs. We're looking into this. Ava, looping you in as the AE and owner of the account; Marissa from Sales Eng will help collect runtime traces and prioritize.

Initial ask from customer: 1) quick mitigation so live notes don't drop segments, 2) a roadmap ask for SDK-level connection affinity or resume semantics so their reconnections are seamless.

Sara, can you confirm the SDK version and whether you're using the JS streaming helper (v2.3.0) or the raw websocket path? Also: is there a consistent client-side pattern that precedes the disconnect (e.g., network blip vs steady high token rate)?

— Logan
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 15:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent streaming disconnects during live notes ingestion

Thanks for the repro, Sara — I ran the script and saw the same behavior. Quick notes from runtime side:

- We observe a short-lived 502 when the request is routed between different runtime pools during a reconnect. The KV cache session gets evicted if the reconnect goes to a different host. That explains the lost partial context and the warm-starts.
- Root cause candidates: (A) connection affinity not being enforced for SDK reconnects, (B) our balanced routing falling back to a different host when the original host is at capacity, (C) client reconnect semantics are opening a new session without a resume token.

Workarounds:
1) On the customer side, reduce connection churn by batching short segments into a single stream where possible.
2) Runtime quick mitigation: temporarily increase stream sticky timeout for the RW-2391 account (can do as an SLA exception for 72 hours) to reduce routing churn.

Proposed product ask (SDK): Add an optional header (X-Redwood-Conn-Affinity) or a resume token that the SDK can persist across reconnect attempts. Runtime can honor the header and route back to the same host or rehydrate KV cache. This would be a medium-complexity change in the SDK (expose token storage and resend on reconnect) and a small change in runtime routing.

I've attached a rough proposal: sdk-sticky-conn-proposal.md and a small trace archive (kvcache_repro.zip).

Can Product weigh in on prioritization? If we implement the header + runtime honor, it should eliminate the warm-starts in most cases.

— Dev
Platform Engineer, Runtime

From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 08:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent streaming disconnects during live notes ingestion

Thanks Dev — that matches what Obsidian is seeing. Marissa, quick ask from AE: can we get the 72-hour sticky timeout change applied as an exception while we scope the SDK change? If legal/SRE are okay with the SLA exception, that will buy time for an engineered fix.

From a product perspective, I'm inclined to treat this as a targeted SDK feature request with a clear cross-team path:
- Short term (<=72h): apply sticky timeout increase for RW-2391 and monitor.
- Medium term (1–2 sprints): SDK optional connection-affinity header + persisted resume token; runtime updated to honor token and rehydrate KV cache on reconnect.
- Long term: evaluate a more robust session-resume API that works across Dedicated and Private deployments.

Marissa — can you collect customer acceptance criteria (what's acceptable latency on reconnect, how many reconnects per hour is tolerable) and confirm whether they can deploy the SDK patch quickly? Logistical note: this feature touches runtime routing and SDK storage APIs; we should plan a canary with a small set of customers first.

— Ava
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Ahmed <sara@obsidianhealth.com>, Samir Khan <samir.khan@obsidianhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent streaming disconnects during live notes ingestion

Quick status update and asks:

- Customer acceptance criteria (from Sara during a call): reconnect should preserve last 30s of decoded context and resume without >200ms additional latency for the first 10s after reconnect. They can tolerate one warm start per hour during the canary.
- Obsidian confirms they can roll SDK changes to staging within 48h and to prod in the following week if we provide a stable patch.
- Action items agreed: 
  1) Platform: apply temporary sticky timeout increase for RW-2391 by EOD Friday (SRE runbook required).
  2) Runtime/Platform: review Dev's sdk-sticky-conn-proposal.md and comment by EOD Wednesday on feasibility and required touchpoints.
  3) SDK: scope work to add optional X-Redwood-Conn-Affinity header and resume token storage. Estimate: 3 dev-days + 1 day for release and tests.
  4) Sales/AE: schedule a canary window and a short rollback plan; Sara will own validation on Obsidian side.

I'll open a HubSpot note and tag the deal RW-2391 with the canary timeline. Putting this in the short-term roadmap and requesting Product sign-off for prioritization.

Attachments: none in this email, but see earlier attachments for repro.

— Marissa
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
